exposure: High provision of mother's own milk (MOM) (>=66% of cumulative prescribed enteral volumes from birth to 36 weeks)
Low provision of mother's own milk (MOM) (<66% of cumulative prescribed enteral volumes from birth to 36 weeks)
outcome: Oxygen saturation to fraction inspired oxygen ratio (SFR) at 36 weeks
cohort: The study included 1041 appropriate for gestational age (AGA) preterm infants born between 24(+0/7) and 31(+6/7) weeks of gestation.
finding: High provision of mother's own milk (>=66% of enteral volume) from birth to 36 weeks was associated with a reduced risk of both bronchopulmonary dysplasia (BPD) and low oxygen saturation to fraction inspired oxygen ratio (SFR) at 36 weeks in AGA preterm infants.
